issues.description: Field 'animals' in class Farm: the problem statement and UML require the farm to maintain its animals using a List implemented as an ArrayList and to initialize that ArrayList in the no-argument constructor. The solution's Farm.java declares the field as 'private Set<Animal> animals' and initializes it with 'new HashSet<>()' (losing List semantics such as ordering and allowing different getter/setter signatures). This mismatch between the specified collection type (List/ArrayList) and the solution implementation (Set/HashSet) will confuse students about the expected field type, constructor initialization, and the signatures of the getter/setter/add methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: update solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java to declare 'private List<Animal> animals;' and initialize it in the no-argument constructor as 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();', and adjust the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if Set semantics are intentional, update the problem statement and UML to specify Set/HashSet and remove the explicit ArrayList instruction so student guidance and solution match.
